# R5 production-worker native witness

This isolated diagnostic adds native storage evidence to the R5 worker regressions. It never replaces the ordinary application entrypoint. Select `r5_metro.cjs` only in a disposable development simulator/emulator job, after running `node .github/native/r5_prepare.cjs`.

The preparation script extracts the current candidate's unchanged setup and deletion worker definitions, signer identity functions and account-session observer. It records the SHA-256 of every containing source module and fails if a selected definition disappears or becomes ambiguous. The generated module is ignored by Git; it is regenerated from the checked-out candidate before Metro starts. The native entrypoint imports the actual current Realm schemas, Realm, MMKV, Redux Saga and native DeviceInfo.

The six-process Maestro flow runs five independent disposable cases and then verifies their persisted counts. Each case tests the production setup worker's offline/error/retry decisions and preservation of its one native wallet; the production deletion workers' live, hidden, canary and archived reference checks; native transaction rollback when a later deletion target is absent; and rejection after an A → B → A session change. Another encrypted Realm remains untouched. The last process reopens all five pairs of files, verifies exact wallet/key counts, and removes the fixtures and its MMKV marker.

The test adapters deliberately control Relay responses, wallet/key generation, dispatch, database selection and the backup local-commit boundary. They persist invalid public sentinel records, with no valid seed, private key, address, network call or remote backup confirmation. These checks cover production worker behavior over native storage. They do **not** establish product navigation, concealed UI, PIN/biometric behavior, account login, cryptographic derivation, genuine protected-backup protocol compatibility, old-schema migration or release readiness. Keep those acceptance rows open until their own executable checks pass.

`keeper-r5-native-evidence.json` contains only fixed scenario/status/limitation identifiers, source paths/hashes/function names and five raw timing pairs. `probe_ready_ms` measures this alternate probe's preparation; `setup_first_wallet_ms` measures the controlled worker's first native synthetic-wallet write. Neither is the full app's cold-start or first-wallet UX latency. The separate full-product measurement flow must supply those user-facing measurements. Native host orchestration must validate this JSON and the unchanged installed artifact identity; a Maestro result alone is insufficient.

Initial source package: based on `c1c4b803039b61b940373c4dc9d08473cf25e042` (core `77b72da29ac5f2cdf3f51c9a0e9f3fd1c2af7238` plus 5.1). Approximately 7.5k changed code/test tokens, two related worker scenario areas. No producer branch, app/native dependency input or release configuration changed.

Actual local checks: six host-only extraction/schema/phase/limitation contract tests PASS; Babel transforms PASS; formatting and whitespace PASS. No native application build or simulator/emulator run was performed for this initial commit. Run the integrated exact candidate through both hosted platforms before assigning native PASS. Physical-device and independent security review evidence remain separate.
